title: Socrates and asking questions
examples: What does it mean to know that I do not know something?
Can asking questions really teach me anything?
How did Socrates use questions to help people think?

explain.say: Today we learn about a very famous thinker named Socrates. He believed that asking questions was the best way to learn.
The Socratic method is a way of thinking through questions. It helps you examine your own beliefs carefully.
For example, if you think courage means fighting, Socrates would ask you what that really means. He would ask you for examples.
Another key idea is knowing you do not know. Socrates famously said that recognizing your own ignorance is the start of wisdom.
In everyday life, when you hear a strong opinion, try using the Socratic method. Ask 'why' or 'how do you know that' to explore it.
A common mistake is accepting the first answer you hear as the final truth. Always question the assumptions people make when they speak.

faq.q: What is the Socratic method exactly?
faq.a: It is a method of questioning designed to stimulate critical thinking. It helps people examine their own beliefs deeply.
asks: How do I use the Socratic method?

faq.q: Why is it important to know that I do not know things?
faq.a: Because admitting what you do not know allows you to actually learn something new. This humility is the start of true wisdom.
asks: What is the value of doubt?

faq.q: Does the Socratic method mean I must disagree with people?
faq.a: No, it means you must explore their ideas thoroughly. The goal is understanding, not just winning an argument.

faq.q: Is this method only for philosophy class?
faq.a: No, you can use it when solving problems in science or even planning a trip. It is a thinking tool for life.
asks: Can I use this in maths?
Is it useful for daily life?

faq.a: He was a very famous philosopher from ancient Greece. He spent his life encouraging people to think critically.

facts: Socrates emphasized self-examination as a key part of a good life.
The Socratic method involves asking a series of questions to expose contradictions in beliefs.
The concept of 'knowing that you do not know' is central to Socratic wisdom.

quiz.say: If someone claims that all birds can fly, and you ask them to explain how a penguin fits that rule, you are using:
quiz.why: This tests the boundaries of their initial statement using questioning.

wrong.0: Deduction moves from general rules to specific conclusions, but questioning is more about exploring definitions.
wrong.1: Assuming means accepting something without proof, which is the opposite of what you are doing.
wrong.2: A conclusion is the final statement, whereas you are in the process of questioning to reach it.

quiz.say: When Socrates said that wisdom begins with knowing ignorance, he meant:
quiz.why: This shows that humility is the necessary first step toward true learning.

wrong.1: This is arrogance, which prevents you from learning anything new.
wrong.2: Stopping questions means stopping the process of self-examination.
wrong.3: Silence can mean agreement, but questioning requires speaking and thinking aloud.

quiz.say: Which action best demonstrates the Socratic method?

options.show: Asking 'What do you mean by that?'
options.say: Asking 'What do you mean by that?'

quiz.why: This question forces the person to define their terms, which is the core of the method.

wrong.0: This avoids the difficult topic rather than exploring it deeply.
wrong.2: This is confrontational and shuts down discussion instead of encouraging it.
wrong.3: The method requires you to help them find the answer themselves.
